title: Designing Writing Assistants for Scientific Figure Captions: A Thematic Analysis
venue: Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on Intelligent and Interactive Writing Assistants (In2Writing 2025)
extended_summary:
This paper examines how researchers use AI-generated captions when writing scientific figure captions, with a focus on understanding the writing process rather than only evaluating caption quality as an output. The authors argue that scientific captions are a complex multimodal writing task because writers must coordinate figures, captions, and surrounding text while also meeting disciplinary and venue-specific norms.

The study analyzes video recordings and interviews from a prior think-aloud caption-rewriting study involving 18 participants from diverse research fields. Participants were shown multiple GPT-4o-generated caption options with different input/output configurations and asked to rewrite captions from their own previously published papers. The analysis uses thematic analysis guided by a design space for intelligent writing assistants.

The paper identifies four main themes: the importance of integrating captions with figures and manuscript text, the way AI can help bridge gaps between language proficiency and domain expertise, the usefulness of multiple AI suggestions for inspiration and comparison, and the need to adapt captions to diverse disciplinary and venue norms. The authors conclude that future caption-writing tools should support stronger manuscript-level context, better customization, more diverse suggestion generation, and more flexible adaptation to writing conventions.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative thematic analysis based on interviews and think-aloud data, not an experimental or randomized evaluation. It provides useful design insights, but it does not meet stronger causal credibility criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests practical benefits for caption writing, especially language support and idea generation, but it reports no quantified learning or performance effect sizes. The impact is therefore promising but unclear in magnitude.

interventions.use_case: AI-assisted scientific figure caption writing using GPT-4o-generated caption suggestions with image+text or text-only inputs, including length constraints, for researchers revising captions in scholarly papers

finding.finding_summary: This paper does not test learning gains directly; instead, it qualitatively analyzes how 18 researchers used AI-generated caption suggestions while rewriting scientific figure captions. Participants reported that the tool helped with linguistic clarity and drafting, especially for non-native English speakers, but also raised concerns about redundancy, discipline-specific norms, and overreliance on repeated suggestions.
finding.measure: Thematic analysis of interviews and think-aloud/video-recorded caption-rewriting sessions
